name: Morro
summary: Forecasting droughts and cyclones, then comparing simulated cloud-seeding interventions.
alt: Four maps comparing precipitation changes under simulated cloud-seeding methods
caption: A comparison of four intervention methods in a simulated Middle East drought.
body: Morro pairs ten-day weather forecasts with a dashboard for comparing possible interventions. It uses GraphCast and NVIDIA Earth2Studio, with classifiers that flag drought severity and cyclone formation.
contribution: I worked on the physics-based perturbation pipeline and trained the Random Forest classifiers used to detect drought severity and cyclone formation. The team built Morro at TreeHacks 2026.
context: Winner of a Stanford Ecopreneurship Sustainability award at TreeHacks 2026. Built with Tej Kosaraju and Kieran P.
limits: This is a hackathon simulation. Changes in a forecast are not evidence that an intervention will work in the real atmosphere.

name: Triton Hub
summary: Canvas assignments, academic email, and personal deadlines in one student dashboard.
alt: Triton Hub demo dashboard showing sample coursework and deadlines
caption: The public demo uses fictional courses and messages; no sign-in is needed.
body: Student deadlines arrive in several places. Triton Hub brings Canvas coursework, announcements, academic email, and a personal calendar into a single workspace.
contribution: I integrated live Canvas data into the assignment and announcement views, and built calendar event persistence and completion tracking with Supabase.
context: Built with Rayirth Dinesh, Siddharth Maddikayala, and shrivassudharsan1.
limits: The public demo uses sample data. Connecting a real student workspace requires separate setup.

name: Arnold
summary: A fitness journal that turns a description of a meal or workout into an entry you can review.
alt: Arnold displaying a meal draft with portions and nutrition estimates
caption: Meal entries are reviewed before they are saved to the journal.
body: Describe what you ate or how you trained, check what Arnold understood, then save the entry. The public showcase includes a food and exercise catalog and keeps journal entries in the browser.
contribution: I extended the team’s hackathon prototype with plain-English meal and workout tracking, USDA food lookup, exercise search, and voice interaction. For the showcase, I rebuilt the review-and-save flow, portion conversion, and mobile layout.
context: The original prototype was built with Shrish, Kenny, and Jello at the MCP AI Agent Hackathon in July 2025. The public repository credits additional contributors.
limits: Nutrition values are estimates. The local demo needs no API keys; live integrations are optional.

name: Wendy
summary: A wedding-planning workspace for venue shortlists, inquiry drafts, and guest RSVPs.
alt: Wendy planning chat with prompts for venue search and guest RSVPs
caption: The showcase uses fictional venues and previews inquiries without sending them.
body: Wendy keeps venue search, guest lists, and planning conversations together. You can set a budget and guest count, shortlist venues, and draft an inquiry using the details already in the conversation.
contribution: I built the venue-search tool, connected it to chat, and implemented the reservation-request workflow that collects event details and drafts an inquiry. I also added a self-contained showcase and a mobile layout.
context: Original team: Thaarak Sriram, Shrish Premkrishna, Aryaman Gandhi, and Kenny.
limits: The demo runs locally with fictional data. It does not send email or make bookings.

name: Solar Registry Screening
summary: An explainable pipeline that turns solar installation records into a ranked shortlist.
body: The pipeline validates registry exports, applies qualification filters, and ranks the remaining installations with explicit scoring rules. Each result includes the points and reasons behind its score.
contribution: I built ingestion and validation, deterministic ranking, optional geospatial enrichment, and reporting. The public example uses five fictional installations and a fixed scoring date so its results can be reproduced.
context: Python, Pydantic, PostgreSQL, and optional model-assisted scoring.
limits: The public repository contains synthetic examples. The scores illustrate a screening method; they are not investment recommendations.

name: DSTL Chat
summary: A small chat application with saved conversations, formatted code, and a local demo.
alt: DSTL Chat showing saved conversations and a Python example
caption: A demo conversation with saved history and formatted code.
body: Built during onboarding at UC San Diego’s Data Science Teaching and Learning Lab, this app lets you start a conversation, ask follow-ups, and reopen it later.
contribution: I extended the lab starter by connecting the React interface to the Python API, adding saved history and new chats, integrating Gemma 3, and rendering Markdown. The showcase adds a key-free demo and retry handling.
context: An extension of the DSTL starter repository, using React, FastAPI, and SQLite.
limits: The demo uses built-in replies. Live Gemma responses require a National Research Platform key.

name: Flask Reddit
summary: A small link-sharing feed with voting, hidden posts, and persistent storage.
alt: A dog-link feed with voting controls and hidden posts
caption: A deliberately small, server-rendered application.
body: A Reddit-style feed for sharing dog links. Submit a URL, vote on a post, or move it into a hidden list and restore it later.
contribution: I extended the DSTL onboarding starter with link submission, ranking, hide-and-restore actions, and SQLite persistence.
context: Python, Flask, SQLite, and server-rendered HTML. Starter code and exercise by the DSTL Lab.
limits: This is a local learning project.
